newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - MATIF aims high on Euro launch.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - MATIF aims high on Euro launch.

text.p: The French futures and options exchange Matif plans to meet the launch of a single European currency, or Euro, with a host of new products to help it retain its market share, a senior exchange official said on Thursday.

"We would like to cover the entire yield curve by completing the existing range of products and preparing for those already traded to be switched into the Euro," Matif deputy managing director Jacques Werren told Reuters.

He said the exchange would convert its existing 10-year Notionnel bond contract and three-month Pibor (Paris interbank offered rate) interest rate futures contract to the Euro in time for the currency's expected launch on January 1, 1999.
"For the international part of fund allocation, which is today not denominated in U.S. dollars, the Euro will certainly be a very strong currency," Werren said.

The launch of Matif's long-term yield spread contracts (LYS) on Friday would open a new product range for the exchange, which could be expanded to include other countries if they did well, Werren said.
Matif is launching four of these contracts initially, based on differences between long-term bond yields in Germany and those of France, Spain, Italy and the United States.
Werren said Matif was not concerned about the dominant position of the London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE) in Europe's short-term interest rate futures market.

The development of a Euribor, or average inter-bank rate offered by European Union banks to prime borrowers, could lead to a situation where investors could trade a Libor futures contract in London and a Euribor futures contract on the continent, he said.

Werren said Matif aimed to boost liquidity in its Euro products by reducing access costs for its customers and offering standard clearing and trading systems through international linkages with other exchanges.

He said Matif was close to finalising a "technology swap" agreement with the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME), under which the U.S. exchange would use an electronic trading system designed by the French stock exchange while Matif would use the CME's clearing system.
The new electronic system would be similar to the currently used GLOBEX screen-based after hours trading system, jointly developed by Reuters Holdings Plc, the CME and Matif.
Reuters said in February that GLOBEX was not likely to continue beyond 1998 as the original partners developed their own systems.
Werren said the new system would feature the same contracts, as the existing CME-Matif link, and would probably even be called GLOBEX.
On possible links with Asian exchanges, Werren said Matif was continuing to hold talks with the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) but it was too early to be sure of the outcome.
"All these discussions may take more time than we expect. SIMEX may want to wait and see what kind of business the Euro will be offering before making any choice," he said.
SIMEX has said it was in talks with LIFFE, Matif and the German futures exchange, the DTB, and hoped to forge a link this year with an eye to trading a contract based on the Euro.
